items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: Nelson's a good man on that but these boys was together.

ctx.x: I was wondering, oh excuse me, the band I heard you in the night before last was George Lewis which had done Preservation Hall. How did that sound compared to this band? Was there

much difference in the music faster, slower? Yeah, lots of difference because the music wasn't that fast so like we played over there, you know what I mean? And you take the trumpet like I told you before, there's no man can fit in there like that boy there. You see what I'm talking about? Nelson's a good man on that but these boys was together. You understand? They'd been working together God knows how long. And this band was just put together. Of course the other night you had a piano too, and there's no piano.…

you know what I mean? There's somebody that'd mess up. Might be out of tune in all the things. Yeah, so we just used like that. We'd take that there and go anywhere. Satisfy anybody. Yeah, them same six pieces you see there. I wonder about your part. Did you play mostly two beat or four beats? Well it was mostly four beats. In those days too. In those days you didn't change your style much.
